newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal shares hit record highs on mkt upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Portugal shares hit record highs on mkt upgrade.

text.p: Euphoria gripped Portugal's stock market on Friday, driving the index and blue chip stocks to new peaks in record volume, after a leading rating agency decreed that the market had finally come of age.

Investors fell over each other to grab stock in expectations of further price gains after Morgan Stanley Capital International, whose views are widely followed by big fund managers, upgraded Portugal from emerging to developed market.
The PSI20 index, which tracks the top 20 blue chips, rose 4.4 percent to close at a record 6,634.69 points.
Turnover on the cash market was also a record 22 billion escudos ($127 million).
But the progress of some individual stocks was even more spectacular, with the country's largest non-state bank, Banco Comercial Portugues, soaring 10.7 percent to close at 2,930 escudos per share.
Portugal Telecom, the biggest company on the market, notched up gains of 4.3 percent while leading retailer Jeronimo Martins JPRN.IN jumped nearly nine percent.
In all, several shares hit all-time highs as investors saw the Morgan Stanley decision becoming a magnet for big money, particularly U.S. pension and investment funds.
"It was just crazy. The buy orders started in the pre-opening session and just never stopped," said one Lisbon trader.
Traders said that the market still had more room to rise, particularly if the international mood remained positive, even if the euphoria seen on Friday could probably not be maintained.
"Many buy orders were left uncompleted. If the mood abroad stays positive, we can see some further gains," said another trader.
Although the Morgan Stanley rating only takes effect on December 2, the market clearly decided that the mere announcement of the intention was enough.

Morgan Stanley said on Wednesday night -- Thursday was a holiday in Portugal -- that progress made in the running of the economy together with the growing size of the local equity market justified the upgrade.

The importance of the move is that many international fund managers, who probably had taken scant notice of the Lisbon market before, will now automatically place part of their portfolios in Portuguese stocks, analysts said.

Besides Telecom, BCP and Jeronimo Martins, retailer and real estate group Sonae Investimentos, Banco Espirito Santo and Banco Portugues de Investimento were amongst other stocks to hit peaks in the hectic trade.
